title: Online Orders Price Adjustment Policy
content:
When the regular site price of the same SKU drops below the unit price the customer paid on an Online Orders order after allocated discounts, the difference is credited to the line.

## Conditions

1. **Window.** A price adjustment is granted only if it is requested no later than the price-adjustment window in calendar days after the order is placed. The window is the price-adjustment window of the customer's Marlowe Rewards tier on the request date, or the base price-adjustment window of 14 calendar days without an open membership. Window days are counted as calendar days after the placed date, the placed date being day zero, and a request on the last day of the window is granted. The placed date is read from the order record and the tier from the customer's Marlowe Rewards membership record.
2. **Reference price.** The reference price must be the regular price shown on the site on the request date. Clearance prices, flash-sale prices and prices reachable only with a code never qualify.
3. **Smallest difference.** The per-unit difference must be at least 1.00, the smallest per-unit difference adjusted on every delivery service.
4. **Once per line.** A line can be adjusted at most 1 time, judged from the line's own adjustment history on the order record, only for units neither cancelled nor returned, and final sale lines are never adjusted.
5. **Where the money goes.** The credit is refunded to the original tenders in the order's refund order of tenders.

## The credit

The credit on a line is the unit price paid after allocated discount less the reference price, multiplied by the units still kept. The unit price paid after allocated discount is the line's net amount spread evenly over its units.

## Window boundary (hypothetical order placed on 2 March 2026, customer without an open membership, window 14 days)

| Request date | Day after placement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2 March 2026 | Day 0 | Within the window |
| 16 March 2026 | Day 14, the last day | Granted on the window condition |
| 17 March 2026 | Day 15 | Outside the window; not granted |

## Worked credit (hypothetical line)

A line of 2 units at 60.00 each carries an allocated promotion discount of 12.00, so its net amount is 108.00 and the unit price paid after allocated discount is 54.00. On the request date the regular site price of the same SKU is 49.00. The per-unit difference is 5.00, which is at least 1.00. One of the two units has been returned, so 1 unit is still kept. Credit: 5.00 multiplied by 1, that is 5.00.

If the regular price on the request date were 53.50 instead, the per-unit difference would be 0.50, below 1.00, and no adjustment would be made.

## Basis questions

**The lower price is a flash-sale price. Does it qualify?** No. Flash-sale prices never qualify as the reference price; neither do clearance prices or prices reachable only with a code.

**A line was adjusted last week and the price has dropped again. Is a second adjustment possible?** No. A line can be adjusted at most once.

**The line was sold as final sale.** Final sale lines are never adjusted, whatever the price difference.

**The customer holds an open Marlowe Rewards membership.** The window is then the price-adjustment window of the member's tier on the request date, not the base window.
